Synthetic difference in differences

Source: R/panel_causal.R
syndid.Rd

Arkhangelsky et al.'s estimator for units adopting a policy at one date: comparison units weighted so their pre-period path parallels the treated units', pre-periods weighted so they predict the post-period, and the difference in differences taken with both weights.

Usage

syndid(data, unit, time, y, ftreat, reps = 200L, seed = NULL, conflvl = 0.95)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit and period.

unit, time, y

Column names: the unit, the period (numeric, for example a year or a month index) and the outcome.

ftreat

Column name of the period a unit is first treated (NA, 0 or Inf for a unit never treated). Treatment is taken as staying on.

reps

Placebo replications (default 200).

seed

Optional seed for the placebo draws.

conflvl

Confidence level (default 0.95).

Value

A list of class rmbl_synthdid: estimate, se, lower, upper, unitwts, tmwts, method ("placebo" or "jackknife"), paths (treated and weighted comparison means by period). plot() draws the paths.

Details

With \(N_0\) comparison units, \(N_1\) treated, \(T_0\) pre-periods and \(T_1\) post-periods, the unit weights solve $$\min_{\omega_0, \omega \in \Delta} \frac{1}{T_0}\sum_{t \le T_0}\Big(\omega_0 + \sum_j \omega_j Y_{jt} - \bar Y_{1t}\Big)^2 + \zeta^2 \|\omega\|^2,$$ with \(\zeta = (N_1 T_1)^{1/4} \hat\sigma\) and \(\hat\sigma\) the standard deviation of the comparison units' first differences before adoption; the time weights solve the same problem across comparison units, predicting each unit's post-period mean from its pre-periods, with \(\zeta = 10^{-6}\hat\sigma\). The estimate is $$\hat\tau = \Big(\bar Y_{1,post} - \sum_t \lambda_t \bar Y_{1t}\Big) - \sum_j \omega_j \Big(\bar Y_{j,post} - \sum_t \lambda_t Y_{jt}\Big).$$ The weights are the exact solutions of these convex problems (the synthdid package runs Frank-Wolfe and then sparsifies, so its estimate differs slightly). The standard error is the placebo one when there is one treated unit (each set of \(N_1\) comparison units in turn treated as if adopting, weights re-estimated), else the jackknife over units with the weights held fixed (Arkhangelsky et al. 2021, algorithms 3 and 4).

References

Arkhangelsky D, Athey S, Hirshberg DA, Imbens GW, Wager S (2021). Synthetic difference-in-differences. American Economic Review 111(12):4088-4118. doi:10.1257/aer.20190159

Examples

p <- polex()
p1 <- p[is.na(p$refmonth) | p$refmonth == 13, ]
syndid(p1, "district", "month", "crmrate", "refmonth", reps = 50, seed = 1)
#> Synthetic difference in differences: -3.126 (jackknife s.e. 0.2474; -3.611 to -2.641)
#> Unit weights: D12 0.203, D16 0.200, D08 0.200, D20 0.199, D04 0.198
